benchmark.description: The W42 benchmark, version 3: the multilingual instrument of the mission's §14.1, grown from the frozen version 1 (the baseline, decision D-001) and from the version 2 candidate. Every item names the workspace it belongs to, whether the system is expected to ANSWER it or to REFUSE it, the terms the answer must mention, the terms it must not, the split it belongs to, and what it measures. The splits are disjoint: the train split is the material a change may be developed against, the validation split is the material a threshold may be chosen on, and the test split is the material the number is reported from. The delayed-recall items test a LESSON item of the train split and are themselves items of the test split, so the lesson set and the recall set are disjoint; the delay is LOGICAL - the recall item is asked after the other items of the run, and the dialogue the lesson happened in has rolled out of the context - and not a wait on the wall clock. The Russian items are cross-lingual by construction: the knowledge packages are in English, so a Russian question asks whether the concept identity survives the language of the question, and the answer it must produce is the English statement the package holds. The key terms of every item are the ENGLISH terms of the package, in both languages.

splits.train: the material a change may be developed against; it holds the lesson items of the delayed-recall pairs
splits.validation: the material a threshold may be chosen on
splits.test: the material the reported number is measured from

provenance.generator: hand-authored from the bundled knowledge packages (knowledge/photosynthesis.pack.json, knowledge/logic.pack.json) and checked against them by the reachability test

generatorParameters.seedScope: the seed of the synthetic typo benchmark this file follows; the misspelled items carry the kind of edit in their notes, so the typo set is reproducible by hand as well
generatorParameters.etalonRule: the etalon of an answerable item is a phrase the knowledge package actually states about the concept the item asks about; a TRANSFER item instead names the instance the question itself states, because that is what the applied rule has to carry
generatorParameters.pointerRule: the workspace of an item is the package that holds the concept the item asks about; a pointer that names a workspace without the concept is a defect in the data (decision D-013) and the reachability test fails the build
generatorParameters.unanswerableRule: the key terms of an UNANSWERABLE item are OUTSIDE the package, and the reachability test fails the build if one of them is inside it
generatorParameters.delayedRecallRule: the lesson item of a recall item is in the train split, the recall item is in the test split, and the two sets are disjoint

provenance.frozenBaseline: benchmark/w42-benchmark-v1.json is the baseline of decision D-001 and is not changed by this file
